status.detail: 10 of 10 sample rows checked (15 Nov); fixes applied report-wide
Aayush is checking a sample now

questions.title: Should a Minor (MN) finding get its own defect row?
questions.context: Inspection tables rate each item ND, MN, MD, MJ or SV. Today the answer key adds a defect row only for MD (Moderate) or worse; an MN item keeps MN as its rating and gets no defect row.
questions.example: Alameda mooring hardware, base rated MN: no defect row. The same base rated MD or S: one defect row.

options.label: A. Keep as is: rows for MD or worse only
options.effect: No change. 104 Alameda mooring bases rated MN stay rating-only.

options.label: B. Add a row for every listed finding, MN included
options.effect: About 104 more Alameda rows. Berkeley pile forms already list 40 MN defects, so B would also make the two reports consistent.

questions.why: This changes what counts as a missed defect when we score Method A and Method B.

questions.title: Is a stated cause its own defect, or a detail of the defect?
questions.context: Reports often name the damage and its cause together. Today the answer key keeps one defect row and puts the cause in a cause column.
questions.example: Berkeley batter pile, "90% SECTION LOSS FROM MARINE BORER": one section-loss row, cause = marine borer. A separate marine-borer row counts as a duplicate.

options.label: A. Keep as is: one row, cause in its own column
options.effect: No change. 644 rows carry a cause (615 Berkeley, 29 Alameda).

options.label: B. Add a second row for the cause
options.effect: Every row with a cause gains a twin, and an extraction that splits them is no longer penalised.

questions.why: Cause matters for forecasting (corrosion-driven cracks behave differently from structural ones), so we want to record it the way Mira would use it.

questions.title: How should "active state of collapse" be labelled?
questions.context: Alameda p.76: "In several areas, the timber fender system is in an active state of collapse"
questions.example: This describes the fender system as a whole rather than one measured defect.

options.label: A. A new defect type, collapse
options.effect: Keeps the report's meaning, but adds a word to the defect list.

options.label: B. An existing type, with the wording kept as severity
options.effect: For example structural damage, severity "active state of collapse".

questions.why: Same question will come up for other system-level failures.

rules.title: Severity is copied word for word from the report.
rules.example: "hairline cracks" stays hairline, never re-labelled minor.

rules.title: A stain or efflorescence note is an attribute of the crack or spall it sits on, not a separate defect.
rules.example: Berkeley VC 1/8"X2' W/CS is one crack, with corrosion stain.

rules.title: No rating word in the report means NR (not reported). Ratings are never guessed.
rules.example: Alameda Pier 3 deck edge (p.38) has no rating word, so NR.

rules.title: An open spall is spalling; a closed spall (delaminated, still attached) is delamination.
rules.example: Applied after the Berkeley check: 89 rows became delamination.

rules.title: On pile tables and forms, each defect takes the pile's rating as its severity.
rules.example: The pile is rated by its worst defect (Alameda Appendix C, Berkeley pile forms).

rules.title: A rust stain on its own is corrosion, with the attribute stain only.
rules.example: Berkeley CS N FACE: corrosion, stain only.
